diagnosis.summary: Checkout‑api latency spiked after the 10:15 PM production deployment of v4.17, causing ConnectionPoolTimeoutErrors and long db acquire spans. The issue was resolved by rolling back the orders‑client upgrade that reduced the connection pool size.
diagnosis.root_cause: The checkout-api release downgraded the orders-db connection pool from 50 to 10 connections and tightened the acquire timeout to 2000 ms, exhausting the pool during peak traffic.

evidence.finding: p95 latency jumped from 200 ms to 2150 ms within minutes of the deployment
212 ConnectionPoolTimeoutError logs in last 15 min with pool max=10, in_use=10, waiting=143
db.pool.acquire span lasted 1829 ms during a slow checkout trace
orders-db pool had max_connections=10, in_use=10, waiting=143, acquire_wait_p95_ms=1800
commit a91f3c2 changed config/database.yaml to set pool.max_connections: 10 and acquire_timeout_ms: 2000

ruled_out: Other services (payment-gateway, inventory-api) had no latency change; logs show only checkout-api errors

proposal.rationale: The incident diagnosis shows that the 10:15 PM deployment of v4.17 downgraded the orders‑db connection pool to 10 connections with a 2000 ms acquire timeout, causing pool exhaustion and a spike in checkout‑api p95 latency. Rolling back to the previous stable release v4.16 restores the original pool configuration (50 connections) and resolves the latency regression.
